generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full: flowers perfect, regular, hypogynous; sepals 6, in 2 circles; petals 6, in 2 circles; stamens as many and opposite them, the anthers opening by uplifted valves; ovary one, superior, 1-celled. Achlys is anomalous, with no perianth and 9 to 13 stamens.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 257 Nandinaceae and 251 Podophyllaceae (his Berberidaceae page is not in this scan), which APG joins with the barberries as Berberidaceae: leaves alternate or basal, simple, lobed or compound; stipules absent; fruit a berry, or a follicle.

traits.leaf_division.note: Wikipedia Berberidaceae (read 2026-10-17): ~700 spp in 18 genera, most of them in Berberis (with Mahonia reinstated as separate). Berberis s.s. (~500, approximate) has simple leaves; compound leaves are in Mahonia (~100, pinnate), Epimedium (~60, ternate), Nandina, Vancouveria, Achlys, Caulophyllum and Leontice. Re-ranks the earlier value, from watson-dallwitz-1992, whose top states were tied.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Wikipedia Berberidaceae (read 2026-10-17): most species are Berberis, whose simple blades are unlobed (entire or spiny-toothed; approximate count ~500). Lobed simple blades are confined to the small podophylloid genera (Podophyllum, Dysosma, Sinopodophyllum, Diphylleia, Jeffersonia; a few dozen spp). Re-ranks the earlier value, from watson-dallwitz-1992, whose top states were tied.

traits.division_pattern.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Berberidaceae with Leonticaceae, Nandinaceae and Podophyllaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves simple often, compound often; the simple blade lobed often, none often; lobes or leaflets palmate often, pinnate often. Read from the coded leaf form and dissection by script (spec-rework/b1/delta).

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 288, family Berberidaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral, usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 288, family Berberidaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 288, family Berberidaceae: life span perennial; read as "perennial".

traits.leaf_margin.note: DELTA, Berberidaceae (read 2026-10-17): margins entire or toothed, teeth usually prickly, lamina often spinose; Wikipedia Berberis: entire or spiny margins; Britannica: spiny-margined leaves. Weighted to Berberis incl. Mahonia, most of the family.
